sentences.text: So far, every steering rule has been about two boats of the same kind.
What happens when a powerboat meets a sailboat, or a sailboat meets a trawler with her nets down?
Rule eighteen answers it with what I call the ladder.
Look at the screen, and read it from the bottom up.
Each vessel keeps out of the way of the vessels above her.
A power-driven vessel underway keeps out of the way of four kinds of vessel: one not under command, one restricted in her ability to maneuver, one engaged in fishing, and a sailing vessel.
Power-driven sits on the bottom rung, and that’s where your charter boat lives.
Most days, almost everything out there that isn’t another powerboat has priority over you.
The logic of the ladder is simple: the less a vessel can maneuver, the higher she stands.
